Request: Percutaneous vertebral augmentation (kyphoplasty), CPT 22514, ICD-10 M80.08XA. Today: 09/22/2026.

Criteria (answer every key):
[fx.acute] Osteoporotic VCF (T1-L5), acute (< 6 wk) or subacute (6-12 wk) from symptom onset. Threshold: {"max_weeks": 12}. Policy text: Acute (< 6 weeks) or subacute (6-12 weeks) osteoporotic VCF
[fx.imaging] Advanced imaging shows bone marrow edema on MRI or bone-scan/SPECT/CT uptake. Policy text: bone marrow edema on MRI or bone-scan/SPECT/CT uptake
[sym.hosp] Hospitalized with severe pain (NRS or VAS >= 8). Threshold: {"min_score": 8}. Policy text: Hospitalized with severe pain (Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) or Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain score ≥ 8)
[sym.moderate] Pain NRS or VAS >= 5 despite optimal non-surgical management. Threshold: {"min_score": 5}. Policy text: moderate to severe pain (NRS or VAS ≥5) despite optimal non-surgical management (NSM)
[sym.worsening] Worsening pain. Policy text: Worsening pain
[feat.progression] Progression of vertebral body height loss. Policy text: Progression of vertebral body height loss
[feat.height] More than 25% vertebral body height reduction. Policy text: 25% vertebral body height reduction
[feat.kyphosis] Kyphotic deformity. Policy text: Kyphotic deformity
[feat.rdq] Severe functional impact: Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire > 17. Threshold: {"min_exclusive": 17}. Policy text: Severe impact of VCF on daily functioning (Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire (RDQ) >17
[care.osteo] Referred for bone density evaluation and osteoporosis treatment program. Policy text: should be referred for evaluation of BMD and osteoporosis education for subsequent treatment as indicated.

    - All patients with VCF should be instructed to take part in an osteoporosis prevention/treatment program
[contra] No absolute contraindication (pain not from the VCF, osteomyelitis/discitis/infection, pregnancy). Policy text: Current back pain is not primarily due to the identified acute or subacute VCF(s).

    - Osteomyelitis, discitis or active systemic or surgical site infection

    - Pregnancy
